angles.name: why it works
angles.writer: explain the psychological or practical reason this idea pays off: what actually changes, in a person or between people, when someone lives it
angles.research: a study (its actual finding, who ran it, and who or how many it studied) or an expert's explanation of why this idea works

angles.name: a common misconception
angles.writer: name what people commonly get wrong about this idea, and show the truer version of it
angles.research: a story or an expert source that corrects a popular misunderstanding of this idea

angles.name: the cost or tension
angles.writer: be honest about what living this idea really costs, or what it competes with, and show why it is still worth it
angles.research: a story of a real person for whom living this idea had a real cost or meant a hard trade-off

angles.name: done well vs. done badly
angles.writer: show the difference between the real practice and its counterfeit (for example, empathy versus people-pleasing), so the reader can tell which one they are doing
angles.research: an example that shows where the line falls between doing this well and a look-alike that goes wrong

angles.name: where it comes from
angles.writer: trace the idea to its roots in a tradition, a thinker, or history, and show what that origin adds to how the reader can practice it today
angles.research: a credible source on the origin or history of this idea (a tradition, a thinker, or a historical moment)

opening: a short scene or moment from a real person's life
a surprising fact or research finding
a vivid everyday situation the reader will recognize
closing: one small action to take today
a question to carry through the day
